Round 1's incrementality findings (a non-kept resolve's records persisting, so a stale stand-in made no auto-global and the incremental program reported a diagnostic a cold compile does not; refresh completion lost across a StatementMemoRetry attempt or an accepted preview), round 1's undirected finding (carried units already fresh for a context change missed the refresh) and round 3's finding (a build that made no program still committed its resolver records) are all instances of it. The corrections now state one rule: every unit record carries the resolve that made it, a resolve counts as kept only when its build commits at the chunk store's commit point beside completeMemos, and the next resolve resolves again every unit recorded after the last committed one; every fresh unit hands its block to the compiler, which takes only blocks it carried. The quality findings (one rescan per block, two lifecycle comments) are closed.
assessment.regressions: One: round 1's correction 00e52531f placed the commit point in compileStory, too broadly, so a build with no program counted its resolve as kept; round 3 found it and 0547bc904 narrows the commit to the build-commit point. The other corrections (df557a02b batching, f6c00cd3f fresh-unit collection, 0dea24227 and f10dd9fcb comments and tests) introduced nothing a later reviewer found. So the mechanism's last behaviour change was itself a correction of a correction, and no independent reviewer has read the invariant in its final form.
assessment.repairOptions: No simpler correct repair is in view. Re-stamping memos without re-resolution was ruled out by the settled decision (a kept chunk does not vouch for the diagnostics a memo replays, #1742). Keying trust to the build commit is the natural invariant; a broader change would reach into how the chunk store commits builds, outside #1974.

A block placed in two places is inspected but not exercised; its failure mode is extra lowering, not wrong output.
